rules.requirement: Prefer safe Rust; model ownership explicitly, borrow instead of cloning unless ownership or measured performance warrants it; no leaking resources for convenience.
rules.evidence: Review lifetime/ownership boundaries and resource-drop tests.

rules.requirement: Isolate unsafe in narrow reviewed modules; document every unsafe operation's safety invariant, provenance, alignment, initialization, aliasing, ABI and lifetime as applicable. Enable unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn lint; forbid unsafe in safe-only crates. Never introduce unsafe solely to appease borrow checker.
rules.evidence: Inventory unsafe incl. generated/native code; reviewer checks invariants; Miri on compatible tests plus native boundary tests.

rules.requirement: Return Result for recoverable failures, Option for absence; propagate with context; no unchecked unwrap/expect/indexing on untrusted input or routine I/O. Justified invariant assertions and tests are permitted.
rules.evidence: Negative tests: malformed input, missing data, overflow, I/O failures; review panic paths.

rules.requirement: Use domain types/enums for invalid-state prevention, explicit units, bounded input, documented public API and minimal visibility; preserve semver contracts.
rules.evidence: API review and doc tests; boundary tests.

rules.requirement: Define lock order, bounded queues, backpressure, cancellation and shutdown. Avoid holding locks across await unless justified; isolate blocking work from async executors and surface task failures.
rules.evidence: Timeout, cancellation, saturation, ordering and shutdown tests; model-check sensitive interleavings where feasible.

rules.requirement: Use rustfmt and Clippy; new warnings fail CI. Suppress individual lints only with reason/scope; do not blanket enable pedantic or suppress all warnings.
rules.evidence: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy for supported targets/features with -D warnings.

rules.requirement: Write unit, integration, regression and doc tests as applicable, including edge cases; use property tests for invariants and fuzz untrusted parsers. Reproduce each fixed bug before/with fix.
rules.evidence: Record commands, seeds, input corpus, outcomes; tests run on intended feature matrix.

rules.requirement: Run pinned-nightly Miri on compatible unsafe/FFI wrapper tests; native sanitizers or hardware tests where Miri cannot execute; do not treat either as proof.
rules.evidence: Miri logs or BLOCKED with alternative and review; no false N/A.

rules.requirement: Declare edition and supported rust-version; pin tested toolchain for release; commit lockfile for applications and CI reproducibility, test dependency resolution for libraries where needed; minimize enabled features.
rules.evidence: Locked builds/tests; MSRV test where claimed; record rustc -Vv and cargo -V.

rules.requirement: Review direct/transitive crates, unsafe and native dependencies, build scripts/proc macros, licenses and advisory findings; avoid unexplained new runtime dependencies. Never run untrusted code with secrets.
rules.evidence: cargo tree, cargo audit, license/provenance review; unresolved material risk blocks release.

rules.requirement: Establish workload, baseline and budget before optimization; measure release builds on equivalent hardware/input; avoid speculative unsafe, allocations or clones; report distributions and regressions.
rules.evidence: Record benchmark commands, toolchain, hardware, repetitions and uncertainty; no universal speed claims.

rules.requirement: Declare supported OS/architectures and feature combinations; isolate platform bindings and native dependencies; validate runtime on supported targets, not merely cross-compile.
rules.evidence: Mac/Linux target matrix and actual runtime evidence; mark unavailable target BLOCKED.

rules.requirement: Use structured logs, error context and bounded telemetry without secrets, personal data or unbounded payloads; validate external inputs and apply least privilege.
rules.evidence: Redaction, limit, malformed input and failure-path tests; security review.

rules.requirement: Independent review for material changes; record commit, policy SHA, commands, target, tests, artifacts/digests, findings and approvals; no claims based solely on compilation.
rules.evidence: Release dossier and PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED per applicable gate; human approval for production.

rules.requirement: For audio/SDR callbacks avoid blocking, allocation and unbounded work; measure overruns and latency. For scientific code specify units, overflow, NaN/Inf, tolerances and reference results.
rules.evidence: Native device/latency tests or numerical reference fixtures; hardware-dependent claims blocked until observed.
